subject: Art & Design
title: Street Art: From Vandalism to Galleries
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Street Art: From Vandalism to Galleries.

hook.text: Banksy shredded his own painting at auction the moment it sold. The price doubled.

buildup.text: Street art started as graffiti in 1970s New York — tags on subway cars, names on walls.

discovery.text: Artists like Basquiat, Keith Haring, and Banksy turned public walls into political commentary.

twist.text: The art world that once arrested graffiti artists now pays millions for their work.

climax.text: Street art is now the most globally accessible art form — no gallery ticket required.

punchline.text: The walls talked. Eventually, the world listened.

quiz.question: How did the art world's view of street art change?
options: From treating it as vandalism to paying millions for it
It was banned in all countries

details.summary: Street art evolved from 1970s graffiti in New York subways to a global art movement. Banksy's political stencils, Shepard Fairey's 'Obey' campaign, and JR's photographic murals transformed public spaces into galleries.
details.whyItMatters: Street art democratized art by removing gallery gatekeepers. It proves that art's power comes from visibility and message, not institutional approval — reaching audiences who would never enter a museum.
takeaways: Evolved from 1970s graffiti to a global art movement
Banksy, Shepard Fairey, and JR are leading practitioners
Once vandalism, now commanding gallery prices worldwide

faq.question: Is street art the same as graffiti?
faq.answer: Graffiti typically focuses on stylized lettering and tags (signatures). Street art encompasses a broader range — stencils, murals, wheatpaste posters, installations, and sculpture in public space. The line is blurry, and many artists work in both traditions.

faq.question: How does Banksy remain anonymous?
faq.answer: Despite worldwide fame, Banksy's identity remains unconfirmed. Works appear overnight, installed by unseen teams. Legal disputes and property sales are handled through representatives. Several journalists have proposed identities, but none have been definitively confirmed.
